name: cefra
description: Manage your private Cefra vocabulary sets and words.

interface.longDescription:
Cefra is a language-learning app for building and training your own vocabulary. This connector lets your assistant work with your private Cefra dictionary while you chat.

Ask it to turn a text, a lesson or a topic into a vocabulary set: it writes the translations, example sentences, articles and verb forms, and Cefra stores them in your account so you can train them on cefra.app. It can also search the curated Cefra catalogue, copy a ready-made set or word into your account, find words you already have, and tidy up sets.

You stay in control. You connect with your Cefra account on Cefra's own consent screen and choose the permissions: reading, adding and changing, and — only if you tick it — deleting. Deleting a set always takes a confirmation, deleted items can be restored through support for 30 days, and daily limits keep runaway edits in check. The connector only sees your vocabulary and the public catalogue: not your profile, your training progress or your conversation. Disconnect at any time under Connected apps in your Cefra profile.

Works with the language pairs of your Cefra account; add a new pair in the Cefra app first.
defaultPrompt: Make a Cefra set "A1 Kitchen" with 10 A1-level German words for the kitchen, with English translations.
Find a German A1 set about food in the Cefra catalogue and copy it to my account.
Add the 10 most useful new words from this text to a new Cefra set, skipping ones I already have.

positive.description: Create a set and fill it
positive.prompt: Create a Cefra set "A1 Kitchen" with 10 A1-level German words for the kitchen, with English translations.
positive.expected_behavior: A new German → English set "A1 Kitchen" is created with 10 words. The reply gives each word's status (created, or added_to_set if the word was already in the dictionary).

positive.description: Copy a set from the public catalogue
positive.prompt: Find a German A1 set about food in the Cefra catalogue and copy it to my account.
positive.expected_behavior: An A1 food set from the catalogue appears among the user's sets. Asking again returns the existing copy instead of creating a second one; the public set itself does not change.

positive.description: Add words to an existing set
positive.prompt: Add "der Bahnhof", "die Fahrkarte" and "der Koffer" with English translations to my set "Demo – Travel".
positive.expected_behavior: The three nouns are added with article and plural. Repeating the prompt adds nothing new: the words come back as already_exists.

positive.description: Rename a set and set its level
positive.prompt: Rename my set "Demo – Travel" to "Travel basics", set its level to A1 and add the description "Words for my trip".
positive.expected_behavior: The set has the new title, level A1 and the description. The reply shows the new title.

The first delete_set call deletes nothing: it returns the set and its word count, and ChatGPT asks the user to confirm. Only after "yes" does a second call with the confirmation token delete the set. Its words stay in the user's dictionary.

negative.description: A language the user is not learning: no words are added because Japanese is not one of the account's language pairs; the reply says new pairs are added in the Cefra app.
negative.prompt: Add 10 Japanese words to my Cefra account.

negative.description: Outside the connector's scope: no tool is called; the reply says the connector manages vocabulary only, not training progress.
negative.prompt: Show me my Cefra training progress and streak.

negative.description: Protected default set: the server refuses because the default set cannot be deleted; nothing changes and the reply says so.

publication.release_notes: First release: manage your private Cefra vocabulary — sets, words and catalogue copies — with read, write and optional delete permissions.
